mean: a story or situation that keeps shifting
lit: turning twice, turning three times: changing direction again and again

use.how: Usually 二転三転する or 二転三転の末: said of plans, statements, explanations, decisions or the lead in a game that change repeatedly. Often a complaint.

near.diff: 朝令暮改 is specifically orders from those in charge being reversed; 二転三転 is any plan, account or situation shifting repeatedly.
急転直下 is one sudden turn that settles things; 二転三転 is shift after shift with no settled outcome yet.

cue: A suspect first says he was at home, then at a friend's, then at work; his account changes each time police question him. What is happening to his statement?

ctx.s: 旅行[りょこう]の計画[けいかく]が{二転三転[にてんさんてん]}して、なかなか決[き]まらない。
ctx.en: Our travel plans keep changing, and we can't settle on anything.

ctx.s: 「結局[けっきょく]、飲[の]み会[かい]は何曜日[なんようび]になったの？」「話[はなし]が{二転三転[にてんさんてん]}して、まだわからないんだ。」
ctx.en: "So what day did the drinks end up on?" "It keeps changing, so I still don't know."

ctx.s: 容疑者[ようぎしゃ]の供述[きょうじゅつ]は{二転三転[にてんさんてん]}している。
ctx.en: The suspect's statement keeps changing.

ctx.s: 試合[しあい]はリードが{二転三転[にてんさんてん]}する、手[て]に汗[あせ]握[にぎ]る展開[てんかい]だった。
ctx.en: The game was a nail-biter, with the lead changing hands again and again.

ctx.s: 新[あたら]しい駅[えき]の建設[けんせつ]予定地[よていち]は、北口[きたぐち]から南口[みなみぐち]へ、また北口[きたぐち]へと{二転三転[にてんさんてん]}した。
ctx.en: The planned site for the new station kept shifting: from the north exit to the south exit, then back to the north.

ctx.s: 説明[せつめい]が{二転三転[にてんさんてん]}するようでは、お客様[きゃくさま]の信頼[しんらい]は得[え]られない。
ctx.en: If your explanation keeps changing, you won't win the customer's trust.

bad.s: 昨夜[さくや]は暑[あつ]くて、ベッドの上[うえ]で{二転三転[にてんさんてん]}した。
bad.en: (meant: it was hot last night and I tossed and turned in bed)
bad.why: It is about plans, statements or situations changing, not physical rolling; tossing in bed is negaeri o utsu.

bad.s: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]してから、私[わたし]の生活[せいかつ]は{二転三転[にてんさんてん]}して、とても良[よ]くなった。
bad.en: (meant: since moving, my life has changed completely for the better)
bad.why: It means repeated reversals, not one big change for the better; say seikatsu ga ippen shita.

mean: the rise and fall of fortunes
lit: flourishing and withering, thriving and declining: like plants, prosperity grows and fades

use.how: A noun, often reflective: 栄枯盛衰は世の常 / 〜の栄枯盛衰を見てきた。 Said over long spans of nations, families, towns, companies or teams.

near.diff: 諸行無常 is the Buddhist truth that nothing at all lasts; 栄枯盛衰 is specifically prosperity followed by decline, often in cycles.

cue: Walking through a mining town that once had cinemas and crowded streets and now stands half empty, you reflect on how it boomed and then emptied out. What do you sense?

ctx.s: どんな大企業[だいきぎょう]にも{栄枯盛衰[えいこせいすい]}はある。
ctx.en: Every great company has its rise and its fall.

ctx.s: 祖父[そふ]は、この商店街[しょうてんがい]の{栄枯盛衰[えいこせいすい]}を七十年[ななじゅうねん]見[み]てきた。
ctx.en: For seventy years my grandfather has watched this shopping street boom and decline.

ctx.s: 「あのゲーム会社[がいしゃ]、昔[むかし]は大人気[だいにんき]だったのに。」「{栄枯盛衰[えいこせいすい]}は世[よ]の常[つね]だね。」
ctx.en: "That game company used to be hugely popular." "Things rise and fall: that's the way of the world."

ctx.s: 世界史[せかいし]の授業[じゅぎょう]で、ローマ帝国[ていこく]の{栄枯盛衰[えいこせいすい]}について学[まな]んだ。
ctx.en: In world history class we studied the rise and fall of the Roman Empire.

ctx.s: 一時代[いちじだい]を築[きず]いた名門[めいもん]チームも、{栄枯盛衰[えいこせいすい]}の波[なみ]には逆[さか]らえなかった。
ctx.en: Even the great team that defined an era could not escape the tide of rise and decline.

ctx.s: 人[ひと]のいなくなった炭鉱[たんこう]の町[まち]を歩[ある]くと、{栄枯盛衰[えいこせいすい]}を感[かん]じずにはいられない。
ctx.en: Walking through the deserted mining town, you can't help feeling how prosperity comes and goes.

bad.s: 朝[あさ]は元気[げんき]だったが午後[ごご]は疲[つか]れて、{栄枯盛衰[えいこせいすい]}な一日[いちにち]だった。
bad.en: (meant: it was a day of ups and downs, lively in the morning and tired by afternoon)
bad.why: It is the long rise and fall of nations, families or businesses, not one person's ups and downs in a day.

bad.s: 彼[かれ]の会社[かいしゃ]は{栄枯盛衰[えいこせいすい]}して、今[いま]では業界[ぎょうかい]一位[いちい]だ。
bad.en: (meant: his company has grown and is now number one in the industry)
bad.why: It includes decline and is a noun, not a verb for growing successful; say kyūseichō shite.
